subtitle: Marble, Faith and Wells in a Fading Kingdom

panels.shot: high, luminous wide shot of Luna Vasahi interior, marble pillars rising like a forest around the brothers
panels.action: Mahamatya Vastupal & Tejpal stand in awe beneath the carved dome of Luna Vasahi, palms joined, tiny against the soaring lattice of white marble pillars that glow in cool temple light.

dialogue.text: As Solanki Gujarat dimmed, two Jain minister-brothers vowed that its light would live on in marble, wells and pilgrim paths.

i18n.hi: जब सोलंकी गुजरात मद्धम पड़ा, दो जैन मंत्री भाई बोले – उसकी रौशनी संगमरमर, कुओं और तीर्थमार्गों में जिंदा रहेगी।

panels.shot: wide aerial of Gujarat, fading sunlight over cities and fields
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of thirteenth-century Gujarat shows fortified towns, temple spires, caravan roads and distant dust clouds, as the sun sinks low over the land.

dialogue.text: In the early 1200s, Gujarat’s glory seemed secure—rich ports, proud temples, the long Solanki line. Yet in its markets, whispers began: new lords were rising, old power was thinning.

i18n.hi: १२वीं सदी के आरंभ में गुजरात अडिग लगा – अमीर बंदर, गर्वीले मंदिर, लंबी सोलंकी वंशरेखा। पर बाज़ारों में फुसफुसाहट थी: नए स्वामी उठ रहे हैं, पुरानी ताकत ढीली पड़ रही है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside a merchant house in Dholka
panels.action: Young Vastupal and Tejpal, in simple yet fine Porwad merchant dress, sit cross-legged in a lamp-lit hall at Dholka, ledgers and grain measures beside them as an elder points to trade routes on a cloth map.

dialogue.text: In Dholka, among Porwad Jain merchants, two brothers learned accounts instead of arms. Vastupal, calm and precise; Tejpal, quick-eyed and restless. Profit was their craft, but faith their compass.

i18n.hi: ढोलका में, पोर्वाड़ जैन सेठों के घर, दो भाई तलवार नहीं, हिसाब सीखते हैं। वस्तुपाल शांत, नापतौल वाला; तेजपाल फुर्तीली नज़र, बेचैन मन। धंधा हुनर, धर्म दिशा।

panels.shot: courtroom wide shot in Patan, with throne slightly off-center
panels.action: In the Vaghela court at Patan, ministers and scribes stand in ordered rows as Vastupal, now mature, presents a scroll to a seated Vaghela ruler; Tejpal stands behind, observing sharply.

dialogue.text: When Vaghela chiefs took the reins from fading Solanki kings, they needed men who could steady revenue, pacify towns, pay troops. The Porwad brothers rose as ministers, not princes, in this new order.

i18n.hi: जब वघेला सरदारों ने ढलते सोलंकी राजाओं से बागडोर ली, उन्हें ऐसे लोग चाहिए थे जो खजाना संभालें, नगर शांत रखें, फौजें चलाएं। पोर्वाड़ भाई मंत्री बने, राजकुमार नहीं, इस नए राज में।

panels.shot: medium shot in council chamber, low-angle toward Vastupal
panels.action: In a wooden-pillared council chamber, Vastupal listens as two local leaders argue, his hand raised for silence, while Tejpal holds a palm-leaf record, ready to note decisions.

dialogue.speaker: Vastupal & Tejpal
dialogue.text: If the kingdom shakes, the poor fall first. Strengthen the ground beneath them.

i18n.hi: राज हिले तो सबसे पहले ग़रीब गिरते हैं। ज़मीन को उनके नीचे से मजबूत करो।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of civic works
panels.action: A composite scene shows labourers digging a stepped well, masons raising a dharmashala, and travellers resting under a shaded colonnade, with Vastupal and Tejpal inspecting the works.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions later speak of their wells, tanks and rest houses—steps cut into earth for water, shelters for weary feet. Civic care, carved into stone, steadied villages more than decrees.

i18n.hi: पटों पर बाद में उनके कुओं, तालाबों, धर्मशालाओं का जिक्र है—पानी को उतरती सीढ़ियां, थके पाँवों को छत। फरमान से ज़्यादा, पत्थर में तराशी नज़ाकत ने गाँव संभाले।

panels.shot: wide shot of Dilwara temples on Mount Abu, dawn light
panels.action: High on Mount Abu, the marble temples of Dilwara sit among dark hills at dawn, Vimal Vasahi’s shrine visible as Vastupal and Tejpal approach with a small Jain entourage and artisans.

dialogue.text: Yet their boldest vow was made on a mountain. At Dilwara on Mount Abu, where Vimal Shah’s temple to Adinatha already gleamed, they planned a shrine to Neminatha that would test the very limits of stone.

i18n.hi: पर उनकी सबसे दिलेरी कसम पहाड़ पर खाई गई। माउंट आबू के दिलवाड़ा में, जहाँ विमल शाह का आदिनाथ मंदिर चमक रहा था, उन्होंने नेमिनाथ के लिए ऐसा देवालय सोचा जो पत्थर की हदें तोड़ दे।

panels.shot: interior planning shot, artisans around a floor plan
panels.action: Inside a temporary wooden hall near the temple site, master sculptors and architects study a drawn floor plan while Vastupal points to the central dome and Tejpal examines a sample block of white marble.

dialogue.speaker: Tejpal
dialogue.text: Let each pillar be a sermon, each ceiling a world.

i18n.hi: हर खंभा एक उपदेश हो, हर छत एक दुनिया।

panels.shot: dynamic construction wide shot under scaffolding
panels.action: Under tall bamboo scaffolds, teams of workers haul and set gleaming marble blocks; a partially carved pillar shows intricate figures emerging as Vastupal and Tejpal look up at the rising Luna Vasahi.

dialogue.text: The Luna Vasahi inscription of 1231 would later fix the date, but in these years all was dust, hammer and chisel. The brothers turned revenue into rhythm, taxes into tracery.

i18n.hi: १२३१ की लूणा वसाही की लेख, आगे चलकर तारीख बाँधेगी, पर इन बरसों में बस धूल, हथौड़े और छैनी थी। भाइयों ने महसूल को ताल में बदला, कर को नक्काशी में।

panels.shot: awe-filled low-angle interior shot of finished dome
panels.action: The completed Luna Vasahi dome rises above, an explosion of finely carved rings; Vastupal and Tejpal stand beneath, heads tilted back, faces lit by soft reflected light from the polished marble.

dialogue.text: When the new Neminatha shrine stood ready, its dome layered like a carved sky, contemporaries called it the crown of Marugurjara art. The inscription named the patrons plainly: Vastupala, Tejapala—ministers, not kings.

i18n.hi: जब नया नेमिनाथ मंदिर तैयार खड़ा था, गुंबद तराशी हुई आसमान की परतों सा, हमख़ासों ने उसे मारूगुर्जर शिल्प का मुकुट कहा। शिलालेख ने यजमान साफ़ लिखे: वस्तुपाल, तेजपाल—मंत्री, राजा नहीं।

panels.action: Priests pour sanctified water over the Neminatha idol as incense curls through the hall; Vastupal and Tejpal kneel, palms joined, as a crowd of Jains watches in silent reverence.

dialogue.text: On consecration day in 1231, chants echoed through the marble forest. The Luna Vasahi inscription bound devotion, art and power together: a Jain merchant-house, serving a Vaghela court, raising a temple that outshone dynasties.

i18n.hi: १२३१ के प्रतिष्ठा दिवस पर मंत्र संगमरमर के जंगल में गूँजे। लूणा वसाही की लेख ने भक्ति, कला और सत्ता को एक डोर में बाँधा: जैन सेठघर, वघेला दरबार की सेवा में, ऐसा मंदिर उठा रहे थे जो राजवंशों को फीका कर दे।

panels.shot: wide pilgrim shot at Girnar, rugged terrain
panels.action: Atop the rugged slopes of Girnar, shrines and steps cling to the hill as Vastupal and Tejpal, with monks and craftsmen, stand near an inscription stone, overlooking the distant plains.

dialogue.text: Soon their names appeared at Girnar too. Inscriptions there, dated 1232, remember Vastupal’s works on that sacred hill—another thread tying their service to the land’s most revered heights.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही उनके नाम गिरनार पर भी दिखे। १२३२ की तारीख वाले पटों में उस पवित्र पहाड़ी पर वस्तुपाल के काम याद हैं—धरती की सबसे पूज्य चोटियों से उनकी सेवा की एक और डोरी जुड़ी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Shatrunjaya hill with temple clusters
panels.action: The terraced rise of Shatrunjaya bristles with temple spires and stone paths, as the brothers watch groups of pilgrims climbing, while workers repair steps and build a rest house near the ascent.

dialogue.text: On Shatrunjaya, where Jain memory ran deep, they funded temples, paths and shelters. Pilgrims climbed more safely now, pausing in dharmashalas that bore the same quiet signature as the great marble halls.

i18n.hi: शत्रुंजय पर, जहाँ जैन स्मृति गहरी थी, उन्होंने मंदिर, पगडंडियाँ, धर्मशालाएँ बनवाईं। अब यात्री ज़्यादा सुरक्षित चढ़ते, बीच-बीच में उन धर्मशालाओं में रुकते जिन पर वही चुप हस्ताक्षर थे जो संगमरमर के महलों पर।

panels.shot: interior library shot with poets and scholars
panels.action: In a shaded hall piled with palm-leaf manuscripts, poets recite as scribes write; Vastupal listens thoughtfully while Tejpal discusses a text with a scholar, a lamp casting warm light on the gathering.

dialogue.text: Their patronage was not of stone alone. Poets like Arisimha wrote of Vastupal’s charity and final pilgrimage. The minister’s house became a literary circle, where Jain and courtly worlds exchanged stories and ideas.

i18n.hi: उनकी सरपरस्ती सिर्फ पत्थर की नहीं थी। अरिसिंह जैसे कवि वस्तुपाल की दानशीलता और अंतिम तीर्थ यात्रा लिखते हैं। मंत्री का घर साहित्यिक मंडली बना, जहाँ जैन और दरबारी संसार किस्से–विचार बदलते।

panels.shot: tense council wide shot with news of threats
panels.action: In a dim council chamber, a messenger, dusty from travel, bows before Vastupal and Tejpal, while a map of Gujarat lies spread, small markers showing unrest near the borders.

dialogue.text: Beyond their circles, threats gathered. Armies moved on Gujarat’s edges, rival chiefs watched the Vaghelas. The Solanki-to-Vaghela change had been slow; the storms now building felt sharper, less forgiving.

i18n.hi: उनके घेरे के बाहर खतरे घिर रहे थे। गुजरात की सीमाओं पर सेनाएँ चल रहीं, प्रतिद्वंदी सरदार वघेलों को तौल रहे थे। सोलंकी से वघेला सत्ता का बदलना धीमा था; अब उठते तूफान तेज, कम रहमदिल लगे।

panels.shot: quiet private medium shot at night, overlooking city
panels.action: At night on a balcony above a lamplit town, Vastupal leans on the parapet in thought while Tejpal stands beside him; distant temple shikharas rise beyond the roofs.

dialogue.speaker: Vastupal
dialogue.text: Rulers pass from ivory seats. Stone, if tended, stands through their passing.

i18n.hi: हाथी-दाँत की गद्दियाँ बदलती हैं। पत्थर, अगर सँवारा जाए, उनके बाद भी खड़ा रहता है।

panels.shot: pilgrimage wide shot on a dusty road
panels.action: On a dusty road lined with sparse trees, Vastupal and Tejpal walk with a small Jain party, carrying simple travel gear; behind them a city fades into haze, ahead a shrine rises faintly on a hill.

dialogue.text: Arisimha’s Vasanta-vilasa remembers Vastupal’s last pilgrimage in the 1240s. The great minister walked as any devotee, leaving courts and ledgers for dust, silence and the long slope toward liberation.

i18n.hi: अरिसिंह की ‘वसंत-विलास’ १२४० के दशक में वस्तुपाल की अंतिम यात्रा याद रखती है। महान मंत्री साधारण श्रावक की तरह चला, दरबार और हिसाब छोड़कर धूल, सन्नाटा और मुक्ति की लंबी चढ़ाई की ओर।

panels.shot: interior close shot of inscription carving
panels.action: A stonecutter carefully chisels letters into a slab, while Tejpal oversees, and the faint outline of Vastupal’s name is visible on the half-finished inscription.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions do not sing, yet they persist. The records at Luna Vasahi and Girnar fix dates and names with quiet certainty, even when later legends embroider costs and miracles around them.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख गाते नहीं, पर टिके रहते हैं। लूणा वसाही और गिरनार के पट चुपचाप तारीख और नाम जड़ देते हैं, भले बाद की कथाएँ उन पर खर्च और चमत्कारों की कढ़ाई क्यों न करें।

panels.shot: present-day-feeling wide shot of Luna Vasahi, empty and serene
panels.action: The Luna Vasahi hall stands quiet and empty, sunlight filtering through the marble filigree; in the imagination, the faint silhouettes of Vastupal and Tejpal seem to watch from the shadows of the pillars.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, dynasties that employed Vastupal and Tejpal are footnotes, but their marble, wells and pilgrim roads still shape Gujarat. They show how patrons can carry a civilization’s craft beyond the fall of its crowns.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, जिन राजवंशों ने वस्तुपाल–तेजपाल को रखा, वे हाशिये की पंक्तियाँ हैं, पर उनका संगमरमर, कुएँ और तीर्थ मार्ग अब भी गुजरात को आकार देते हैं। वे दिखाते हैं कि संरक्षक कैसे ताज गिरने के बाद भी किसी सभ्यता की कला को आगे ढो सकते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Vastupal and Tejpal Keep the Flame
title_i18n.hi: वस्तुपाल और तेजपाल ने ज्योति बचाई

subtitle_i18n.en: Marble, Faith and Wells in a Fading Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर, श्रद्धा और कुएं, ढहते राज में
